paragraphs: Grace and Hope Groups – October 2026
2026 Theme: Living a Life with PurposeSermon Series: Why We Do What We Do - The Meaning Behind Our Worship
How the Meeting Works
The leader reads each question aloud. Everyone takes a turn to answer honestly. What is shared in the group stays in the group. The leader offers a short summary after each round.
This is not meant to be a complicated Bible study. It is a time for conversation, reflection, encouragement, and learning how to follow Jesus together in everyday life.
Opening Prayer
Father, thank You for bringing us together today. Thank You for every woman in this group and for the different stories, experiences, joys, struggles, and responsibilities represented here.

As we think about the things we do in worship, help us understand that they are more than habits or traditions. Teach us why we gather, why we confess our faith, why we pray together, why we use signs such as light, and why we respond to Your goodness with praise and thanksgiving.
Open our hearts so that what we do on Sunday helps shape the way we live every day. Help us know You more deeply and worship You with understanding, gratitude, and sincerity.
In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Scripture Reading
Psalm 95:1–3

Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout aloud to the Rock of our salvation. Let us come before him with thanksgiving and extol him with music and song. For the LORD is the great God, the great King above all gods.
Ephesians 5:8–10

For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Live as children of light (for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness, righteousness and truth) and find out what pleases the Lord.
Leader
This month we are looking at some of the things we do every week in worship and asking a simple question: Why do we do them?

Sometimes we can repeat words, sing songs, pray prayers, or participate in traditions for many years without stopping to think about what they mean. These practices are not meant to be empty routines. They help us remember who God is, what Christians believe, how Jesus taught us to pray, and how our worship should shape the way we live.

The four messages we are considering today help us see that worship is not only something we attend. Worship teaches us, forms us, reminds us, and sends us back into the world to live as God’s people.
Today we are going to focus on four truths.
Four Truths Behind Our Worship
1. Worship reminds us who God is and who we are

Leader:Psalm 95 invites God’s people to sing, give thanks, bow down, and recognize the Lord as their God. In 1 Peter, Christians are described as people who belong to God and are called to declare His praises. Worship is not simply the music before the sermon or a weekly event we attend. It is our response to God because He is worthy, and it reminds us that our lives belong to Him. When we worship together, we remember that we are part of God’s people and that our faith should continue after the service ends.
STOP – THINK – MEDITATE: 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:
When worship becomes familiar or routine, what can help you remember who you are actually worshiping and why?
2. The Apostles’ Creed helps us remember and confess what we believe

Leader:In Deuteronomy, God told His people to remember His words and teach them carefully to the next generation. In 1 Corinthians 15, Paul reminded the church of the gospel he had received and passed on: that Christ died for our sins, was buried, and was raised. The Apostles’ Creed serves a similar purpose in Christian worship. A creed is a short statement of belief. When we say the Apostles’ Creed, we are not praying to the Creed or replacing the Bible. We are using shared words to confess the central faith Christians have received and passed down through generations. Saying it together reminds us that Christianity is bigger than our individual opinions or experiences.
STOP – THINK – MEDITATE: 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:
Why do you think it is helpful to say out loud what we believe instead of only keeping our faith private?
3. The Lord’s Prayer teaches us what matters when we pray

Leader:When Jesus’ disciples asked Him to teach them to pray, Jesus gave them a pattern. The Lord’s Prayer begins by turning our attention toward God: His name, His kingdom, and His will. Then it teaches us to bring our daily needs to Him, receive and extend forgiveness, and ask for help when we face temptation and evil. When we pray this prayer together in worship, we are not simply repeating familiar words. Jesus is teaching us what a God centered life looks like. Prayer includes worship, dependence, forgiveness, obedience, and trust.
STOP – THINK – MEDITATE: 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:
Which part of the Lord’s Prayer is easiest for you to pray sincerely, and which part is more challenging?
4. The candles and Doxology remind us to carry worship into everyday life

Leader:Light is an important picture in Scripture. Ephesians teaches that because we belong to the Lord, we are to live as children of light. In our worship, the candles and the acolytes carrying the light can remind us of Christ and of our calling to live differently because we belong to Him. When the light is carried out at the end of worship, it can remind us that our faith does not stay inside the church building. The Doxology is a short song of praise to God. We often sing it as we offer our gifts, reminding us that everything we have comes from God and that our response is gratitude, praise, and faithful living.
STOP – THINK – MEDITATE: 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:
What would it look like for you to “carry the light” of Christ into one ordinary place in your life this week?
How can gratitude change the way we think about our time, abilities, money, and other blessings?
Final Group Question

Leader:These parts of worship may look different from one another, but they all point us toward the same purpose. Worship helps us remember who God is, confess what we believe, learn how to pray, give thanks for what God has given us, and live as His people beyond Sunday morning.
Take a moment and think about everything we have discussed.
Which of these four areas speaks most to where you are right now: worshiping with greater understanding, knowing what you believe, growing in prayer, or carrying your faith into everyday life? Why?
Leader

Thank you for sharing. We do not have to understand every part of worship all at once. As we learn why we do what we do, familiar practices can become meaningful reminders of God’s grace and of the life He is calling us to live.
As we leave, remember this simple question:
How can what I do in worship shape the way I live this week?
Closing Prayer
Father, thank You for this time together and for every woman who shared today. Thank You for giving us ways to remember Your goodness, confess our faith, pray together, and respond to Your blessings.

Keep our worship from becoming empty routine. When we sing, help us remember who You are. When we confess our faith, help us believe and live what we say. When we pray, teach us to seek Your will, depend on You, forgive others, and trust You with our needs. When we see the light and sing our praise, remind us to carry our faith into the world with gratitude and love.
Help us encourage one another and continue growing together. May the worship we offer with our words become visible in the way we live this week.
In Jesus’ name, Amen.

paragraphs: Grace and Hope Groups – September 2026
2026 Theme: Living a Life with PurposeSermon Series: Meals with Jesus
How the Meeting Works
The leader reads each question aloud. Everyone takes a turn to answer honestly. What is shared in the group stays in the group. The leader offers a short summary after each round.
This is not meant to be a complicated Bible study. It is a time for conversation, reflection, encouragement, and learning how to follow Jesus together in everyday life.
Opening Prayer
Father, thank You for bringing us together today. Thank You for every woman in this group and for the different stories, experiences, joys, struggles, and responsibilities represented here.

As we talk about Jesus and the people He met around tables, help us see that You also meet us in the ordinary places of our lives. Give us hearts that are open to change, willing to receive Your forgiveness, courageous enough to make things right, and humble enough to serve others.
Speak to each of us today and help us take one more step toward becoming the women You are calling us to be.
In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Scripture Reading
Jesus answered them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
“Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet. I have set you an example that you should do as I have done for you.”
Leader
This month we are looking at several meals and encounters Jesus had with people.

Meals may seem ordinary, but in the ministry of Jesus, the table often became a place where something important happened. People were welcomed. Sinners were forgiven. Lives were changed. Pride was challenged. Relationships were restored. And Jesus taught His followers a new way to live.
The four stories we are considering today teach us something important: an encounter with Jesus should change more than what we believe. It should begin changing the way we live.
Today we are going to focus on three truths.
Three Truths from Meals with Jesus
1. Jesus gives us new life and new ways

Leader:Jesus called Levi, a tax collector, to follow Him. Later, Jesus used the picture of new wine needing new wineskins to teach that following Him brings change. Jesus does not only forgive our past; He continues changing our hearts, habits, attitudes, and priorities.
STOP – THINK – MEDITATE: 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:
What makes change difficult for you, even when you know the change may be good?
2. Forgiven people learn to love differently

Leader:While Jesus was eating at Simon’s house, a woman with a sinful past came to Him with tears and anointed His feet. Simon judged her, but Jesus received her with grace. Jesus taught that when we understand how much we have been forgiven, it changes the way we love and see others.
STOP – THINK – MEDITATE: 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:
Why do you think we sometimes find it easier to see another person’s faults than our own?
3. Real change becomes visible

Leader:Zacchaeus was a wealthy tax collector who had treated people unfairly. After meeting Jesus, he decided to give generously and repay people he had cheated. His encounter with Jesus did not only change what he believed; it changed what he did.
STOP – THINK – MEDITATE: 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:
Why is saying “I’m sorry” sometimes easier than actually changing our behavior?
Is there an area where God may be asking you not only to pray about something, but to do something?
4. Jesus shows us how to serve

Leader:At the Last Supper, Jesus washed His disciples’ feet, a job normally done by a servant. Jesus showed them that following Him means humbly loving and serving others. We do not serve to prove our worth or please everyone. We serve because Jesus first loved and served us.
STOP – THINK – MEDITATE: 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:
What makes serving others difficult sometimes?
Who might God be placing in your life for you to encourage or serve this week?
Final Group Question
Leader:These four meals show us people being changed by an encounter with Jesus. Jesus invites us to receive His grace, allow Him to change us, make our faith visible, and share His love with others.
Take a moment and think about everything we have discussed.
Which of these four areas speaks most to where you are right now: changing, forgiving, making something right, or serving? Why?
Leader
Thank you for sharing. None of us has everything figured out. We learn from Scripture, but we also learn by listening to what God is doing in one another’s lives.
As we leave, remember this simple question:
What is Jesus teaching me, and what can I do with it this week?
Closing Prayer
Father, thank You for this time together and for every woman who shared today. Thank You for meeting us with grace and continuing to change us.

Help us recognize the areas where You are calling us to grow. Teach us to forgive because we have been forgiven, to make our faith visible through our actions, and to love and serve others as Jesus has loved and served us.
Help us encourage one another and continue growing together. Take what we have learned today and help us live it this week.
In Jesus’ name, Amen.

paragraphs: Grace and Hope Groups August 2026
2026 Theme: Living a Life with PurposeSermon Series: Purpose in the Everyday: Faith Where You Are
How the Meeting Works:

Leader reads each question aloud. Everyone takes a turn to answer honestly. What is shared in the group stays in the group. The leader offers a short summary after each round. This is not a Bible study. It is conversation, reflection, and learning to walk faithfully together.
Opening Prayer:

Father, thank You for bringing us together this month. Thank You because our daily life matters to You. Teach us to see our work, our homes, our rest, our responsibilities, and even our tiredness through Your eyes. Help us live with purpose in the ordinary places where You have placed us. Give us integrity under pressure, peace in our homes, wisdom to rest, and strength to remain faithful for the long journey. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Scripture Reading
Colossians 3:17, 23–24; Galatians 6:9
17And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.

23 Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters, 24 since you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as a reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
9 Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
Leader:

This month’s sermons remind us that purpose is not only found in big moments. God meets us in daily work, repeated responsibilities, family life, rest, pressure, and long seasons of faithfulness. The world often treats ordinary tasks as burdens, but Scripture teaches us that when we belong to Christ, even the most normal parts of life can become worship.
Three Truths About Living with Purpose in Daily Life
1. God gives purpose to ordinary work

Leader: The Bible begins by showing us that work was part of God’s good plan from the beginning. Before sin entered the world, God placed Adam in the garden with responsibility. He was called to care for what God had created. This means work was not originally given as punishment. Work was created as part of a meaningful life with God.

Later, Scripture teaches that whatever we do can be done in the name of Jesus. This means our daily responsibilities are not separate from our faith. Paid work, housework, caregiving, volunteering, ministry, errands, cooking, cleaning, planning, serving, and organizing can all become ways to honor God.
For many men, daily work can feel repetitive, exhausting, or unnoticed. But God sees what others overlook. When we do our work for Him, even ordinary tasks can become acts of worship.
Application:Think about one responsibility in your life that feels heavy, boring, or unappreciated. Ask God to help you see it as a place where you can serve Him with purpose.
STOP THINK MEDITATE 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:Where do you need to remember that your daily work matters to God?
2. Faithfulness is tested in pressure, home, and rest

Leader: The Bible gives us examples of people who stayed faithful even when life became difficult. Daniel was a man who lived with integrity. Even when others watched him closely and tried to find something wrong in his life, they could not find fault in his character. His faith was not only something he talked about; it was seen in the way he lived every day.

Scripture also teaches that faith must be practiced inside the home. God calls His people to live with compassion, kindness, humility, patience, forgiveness, and love. Sometimes the hardest place to live our faith is not at church, but with the people closest to us.

The Bible also teaches that rest is a gift from God. Rest reminds us that we are not in control of everything. We do not have to prove our worth by staying busy all the time. In a culture that celebrates exhaustion, choosing healthy rest becomes an act of trust in God.
Application:Ask yourself where your faith is being tested right now: at work, at home, in relationships, in your schedule, or in your need to rest.
STOP THINK MEDITATE 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:Where is God asking you to practice faithfulness right now: through integrity, patience, forgiveness, or rest?
3. God strengthens us for the long journey

Scripture speaks honestly about weariness. It recognizes that even doing good can become tiring. Serving, caring, working, forgiving, praying, leading, and showing up can all become exhausting when the season is long.

The Bible also gives the example of Nehemiah, who had an important work to finish. He faced distractions, pressure, fear, and opposition, but he stayed focused because he knew the work God had given him mattered.

God does not ask us to sustain our purpose by human strength alone. Scripture reminds us that unless the Lord builds the house, our labor is empty. We need God to strengthen what we cannot carry by ourselves.
Application:Name one area where you feel weary. Invite God to renew your strength and remind you that faithful effort in His name is never wasted.
STOP THINK MEDITATE 30 to 60 seconds
Then share:Where do you need God to help you not give up?
Group Sharing: Main Questions
1. What ordinary part of your life has God been asking you to see with new purpose?
This could be work, home, family, caregiving, service, ministry, or daily responsibilities.
STOP THINK MEDITATE 30 to 60 seconds
Then share with the group.
2. What pressure or weariness has been testing your faith lately?
This could be stress, burnout, conflict, feeling unseen, disappointment, or carrying too much.
STOP THINK MEDITATE 30 to 60 seconds
Then share with the group.
3. What one practical rhythm would help you live with purpose this week?
This could be resting, praying before work, forgiving someone, asking for help, setting a boundary, encouraging your family, or doing one task for the Lord instead of for approval.
STOP THINK MEDITATE 30 to 60 seconds
Then share with the group.
Leader:

A life with purpose is not only lived in big spiritual moments. It is lived in the kitchen, at the desk, in the car, at church, in conversations, in responsibilities, in rest, and in the quiet decisions no one else sees. God is present in the ordinary. When we work for Him, rest in Him, build our homes on Him, and continue by His strength, our daily life becomes worship.
Thank you for sharing. God is working in each life here. Your work matters. Your home matters. Your rest matters. Your faithfulness matters. Nothing done for the Lord is wasted.

Closing Prayer: Father, thank You for reminding us that our ordinary lives are sacred to You. Help us work with purpose, live with integrity, care for our homes with love, and rest without guilt. Strengthen every man here who feels tired, unseen, or discouraged. Teach us to depend on Your Spirit instead of our own strength. Help us not grow weary in doing good. Build our lives, our homes, and our faith on Christ. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
